facts: Q4 2025 total revenue was $82.4 million, a decrease of 1.3% year-over-year, a meaningful improvement from the double-digit decline experienced in Q3.
Q4 consumables revenue grew 1.7% year-over-year to $57.7 million, while device revenue declined 7.9% year-over-year to $24.7 million.
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA increased 268% to $45.1 million from $12.3 million in 2024, with Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $15 million versus $9 million in the prior year quarter.
Full year 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $285 million to $305 million and adjusted EBITDA of $35 million to $45 million, with Q1 2026 revenue expected at $63 million to $68 million.
The company ended 2025 with an installed base of over 36,000 systems globally, having placed 1,032 delivery systems in Q4 compared to 1,087 in the prior year period.
Adjusted gross margin for the full year 2025 improved from 62% to over 68%, while GAAP gross margin increased from 54.5% to 65.3%.

The company ended 2025 with approximately $232.7 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, down 37% from $370.1 million at the end of 2024, primarily due to repurchase of convertible senior notes.
Q4 churn rate improved to approximately 1.1%, down from approximately 1.8% in Q3, with churn driven mostly by smaller accounts without assigned business development managers.
A next-generation Hydrafacial device is in early stages of development with a planned launch in 2028, designed to drive upgrades across the installed base.
The first half of 2026 is expected to be down mid-single digits year-over-year, with the company expecting to return to revenue growth in 2027 as commercial and innovation initiatives scale.
Q2 total net revenue declined approximately 5% year-over-year, driven by unfavorable weather conditions that negatively impacted visitation and ancillary spending.
Q2 resort reported EBITDA declined approximately 8% compared to the prior year, partially offset by disciplined cost management and Resource Efficiency Transformation Plan savings.

Season-to-date skier visitation through March 1 declined approximately 12%, with even the most committed pass visitation down approximately 14% and non-pass lift ticket visitation down approximately 6%.
Fiscal 2026 resort reported EBITDA guidance was reduced to a range of $745 million to $775 million, roughly $100 million below initial expectations, entirely due to weather impacts.
Rockies snowfall this season is approximately 40% lower than fiscal 2012, which was historically the year with the most unfavorable weather conditions until now.

The company now expects to exceed its initial $100 million annualized Resource Efficiency Transformation savings target by approximately $6 million by end of fiscal 2026, with approximately $42 million of incremental savings in fiscal 2026 before approximately $15 million of one-time operating expenses.
Pass holders now make up approximately 75% of annual visitation, with pass units having grown 55% over the past 5 years, providing meaningful stability in a challenging weather year.

The company introduced new pricing for skiers and riders ages 13 to 30 at 20% less than standard pricing, while announcing 3% to 4% blended price increases on Epic and Epic Local passes before taxes, plus passing through an approximately 3% sales and lift tax on multi-resort passes.

The balance sheet ended the quarter with approximately $1.1 billion in liquidity and net leverage of 3.1x trailing 12-month EBITDA, after retiring $525 million in convertible debt using proceeds from a delayed draw term loan and cash on hand.

The company maintained the quarterly dividend at $2.22 per share and repurchased 0.3 million shares for a total of $45 million year-to-date, while reaffirming calendar year 2026 total capital spending of $234 million to $239 million.
Revenue grew 38.5% year-over-year to $19.4 million, marking the company's 13th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth.
New student starts increased 31.6% to 1,117 students, driving ending student population up 37.7% to an all-time high of 3,495 students.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 9.6% to $3.1 million, while adjusted EBITDA margin declined to 15.9% from 20.1% a year ago due to front-loaded investments in growth.
Diluted EPS fell to $0.16 from $0.21 last year, primarily due to diluted share count increasing from 9.8 million to 13.9 million following the September 2024 IPO.
The company recorded a bad debt reserve of $178,000 (0.9% of revenue) this quarter, in line with expectations, following a $700,000 reserve in Q4 fiscal 2025.
Cash position stands at $20.6 million with only $700,000 in debt, positioning the company for organic growth and M&A opportunities.
Four new programs (MRI, cardiac sonography, surgical technology, and sterile processing) have been approved but not yet launched, with contributions expected in Q2 and beyond.
Contra Costa Medical Career College, acquired in December 2024, has grown to over 500 students and received vocational nursing program approval.
Operating cash flow decreased to $1.1 million from $3.2 million last year, primarily due to timing of Title IV disbursements.
Management expects to announce an M&A transaction within the current fiscal year, with the pipeline elevated to Board-level review for both California and out-of-state multi-campus acquisitions.
PACCAR achieved Q3 2025 revenues of $6.7 billion and net income of $590 million.
PACCAR Parts achieved record quarterly revenues of $1.72 billion with pretax income of $410 million, representing 4% year-over-year growth.
PACCAR Financial Services pretax income was $126 million, an 18% increase over the $107 million reported in the same quarter last year.
Q3 2025 Truck, Parts and Other gross margins were 12.5%, with Q4 margins expected to decline to approximately 12% as tariffs peak in October.
PACCAR estimates the 2025 U.S. and Canadian Class 8 market at 230,000-245,000 trucks, and the 2026 market at 230,000-270,000 trucks.
Tariffs created a $75 million headwind in Q3 2025, with management expecting tariff costs to peak in October before declining through Q4.
Peterbilt and Kenworth combined market share stands at 30.3% in the U.S. and Canadian Class 8 market.
PACCAR delivered 31,900 trucks in Q3 2025 and anticipates delivering approximately 32,000 trucks in Q4 2025.
Q3 2025 truck pricing was down 1.3% year-over-year while costs increased 4.6%, resulting in a negative 5.9% price-cost spread.
PACCAR's Q4 order book is approximately 60-70% full, which is uniform across both North America and Europe.
Full year 2025 total revenue was $35.1 million compared to $37 million in 2024, a decrease of 5.2%.
The company ended 2025 with over 6,700 contracts in baseline assets, representing same-store contract parking growth of 10% year-over-year (12% excluding Detroit disruption).
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $14.3 million compared to $15.8 million in 2024, while Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $3.9 million, flat year-over-year.
The company sold or is under contract to sell over $30 million of noncore assets at an aggregate cap rate of approximately 2%.

2026 revenue guidance is $35 million to $38 million, with adjusted same-portfolio growth of approximately 8% at the midpoint; NOI guidance is $21.5 million to $23.0 million (approximately 10% adjusted growth); and adjusted EBITDA guidance is $15.0 million to $16.5 million (approximately 13% adjusted growth).
The company completed a $100 million asset-backed securitization with 3 new institutional investors in Q3, extending maturities and enhancing flexibility.
Total debt outstanding decreased to $207.7 million as of December 31, 2025, from $213.2 million a year earlier, including approximately $10 million paid down on the line of credit in Q4.
The company has repurchased over 1.6 million shares at an average price of $3.25 per share to date.
Residential parking contracts increased approximately 60% year-over-year in 2025, while transient volumes declined 6% year-over-year.
Full year 2025 net operating income was $20.7 million compared to $22.6 million in 2024, with same-location RevPAS declining 4.7% to $199 from $209.
Q1 2026 revenue reached $462.8 million, a 3.4% year-over-year increase, with Environmental Services at $208.3 million (12.1% margin) and dietary services at $254.5 million (9% margin).
Net income was $26.1 million and diluted EPS was $0.37, supported by a favorable Q1 cost of services ratio of 83.6% versus the company's 86% target.

Workers' comp and general liability efficiencies contributed roughly $4.7 million (about 1% of the 2% cost-of-services outperformance), but management cautioned these benefits are lumpy and unlikely to repeat consistently.
Bad debt expense fell to $3.8 million (under 1% of revenue), down from a recent 2%+ level and a normalized historical range of 1% to 1.5%.
Management guided Q2 2026 revenue of $465 million to $475 million and reaffirmed full-year mid-single-digit revenue growth, implying high-single-digit growth is needed in the second half.

The company repurchased $24 million of stock in Q1 (only $15.3 million under the new $75 million/12-month program), leaving 9.2 million shares under authorization while pursuing a uniform, non-front-loaded cadence.

HCSG ended the quarter with $214.6 million in cash and marketable securities and an undrawn $300 million revolving credit facility, whose maturity was extended to 2031 on April 7 with improved pricing and covenant terms.

The campus segment represents over $100 million of annualized 2025 revenue (less than 10% of total company revenue), and management is targeting small bolt-on M&A deals of $20 million to $30 million purchase price as land-and-expand platforms.

Genesis facilities continue receiving services without payment or operational disruption; the bankruptcy court approved a sale to 101 West State Street, with closing likely pushed to later summer pending a late-April financing commitment.

SNF occupancy remains steady at around 80% across geographies and facility types, and management reported no observed direct on-invoice impact from global energy or supply-chain volatility and no ERC benefit to the P&L this quarter.
Q3 2025 sales of $1.4 billion were up 7% versus prior year, with revenue growth across all reporting segments for the first time since Q1 2022.
Adjusted EPS of $0.97 was down $0.20 year-over-year, with approximately $0.70 of negative impact from reinstated variable compensation and incremental tariffs.
Year-to-date free cash flow reached $355 million, an improvement of $348 million over the first three quarters of 2024, with record trailing 12-month free cash flow of $635 million.
Mercury maintained U.S. outboard market share leadership at 49.4% in Q3, with U.S. engine pipelines down 25% for under 175HP and 33% for over 175HP engines since January 1, 2024.
The company recorded a $323 million noncash intangible asset impairment charge for the Navico Group related to the current trade and economic environment.

Full year 2025 guidance remains unchanged at approximately $5.2 billion revenue, 7% adjusted operating margins, and $3.25 adjusted EPS, with free cash flow guidance raised to in excess of $425 million.

The company increased its 2025 debt reduction target to $200 million (up $75 million since year start) and plans to retire $200 million or more of debt in 2026 while maintaining $1.3 billion in liquidity.
Net tariff impact estimate increased slightly to approximately $75 million for 2025, primarily due to expanded Section 232 tariff scope on aluminum and steel.
Global dealer boat inventory pipelines are down over 2,200 units versus Q3 2024, with U.S. pipelines down over 1,200 units year-over-year.

For 2026, management's preliminary outlook assumes flat to slightly up U.S. retail boat market, with expectations of mid- to high single-digit percent revenue growth and more than 25% growth in adjusted EPS.

Prior year loss and LAE reserves were increased by $38.2 million (2.8% of net unpaid loss and LAE), with accident year 2024 increasing by $40.5 million, accident year 2023 increasing by $16.1 million, and accident years 2022 and prior decreasing by $18.4 million.
The accident year 2025 loss and LAE ratio was increased from 69% to 72% due solely to increased frequency of California cumulative trauma claims.
Gross premiums written increased 1.4% to $183.9 million compared to $181.2 million in the prior year, driven primarily by renewal business premium growth.
The company announced a $125 million debt-funded recapitalization plan and increased its share repurchase authorization by $125 million, expanding total authorization to $250 million.
The underwriting expense ratio decreased to 20.6% from 23.5% in the prior year quarter, primarily due to lower compensation expenses including reductions from an August reorganization.
The company repurchased $45.2 million of common stock during the quarter at an average price of $43.09 per share, representing a 17% discount to adjusted book value per share.
The Federal Home Loan Bank borrowing facility used to initially fund the recapitalization plan has a fixed interest rate of 3.7%.
Adjusted net loss was $25.5 million for the quarter compared to adjusted net income of $20.2 million in the prior year quarter.
Book value per share including deferred gain increased 6.1% to $49.70 and adjusted book value per share increased 5.5% to $51.31 over the last 12 months.
The company is launching a new excess workers' compensation product, with plans to start accepting submissions in early 2026 and binding by July 1, 2026.
Full year 2025 revenue was $120.5 million, representing nearly 9% year-over-year growth, with Q4 revenue of $34.4 million up nearly 22% year-over-year.
GAAP net income for 2025 was $10.8 million, a year-over-year increase of more than 37%, marking the company's first full year of positive EPS ($0.10) since its 2014 IPO.
Non-GAAP free cash flow reached approximately $20.5 million for 2025, a 55% increase over 2024's $13.2 million and representing growth of more than 500% from 2023.

The company's 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $128 million to $132 million, adjusted EBITDA of $29 million to $31 million, and GAAP EPS of $0.20 to $0.23, representing more than 100% EPS growth over 2025, with no unannounced acquisitions included.

Approximately 80% of Series A preferred shares were converted to common during 2025, eliminating more than $7 million in annual dividend obligations, and the Provident Bank credit line was fully repaid, leaving $10 million available and undrawn.

All four 2025 acquisitions were executed at less than 1x revenue multiples, funded entirely through free cash flow with zero common shareholder dilution, including the Medsphere Systems acquisition which contributed approximately $7.2 million in Q4 revenue.

The stratusAI Front Desk Agent, commercially launched in December 2025, addresses an estimated $4 billion-plus market opportunity and is already handling nearly 80% of inbound scheduling-related calls at one client site (The Lung Center).

The company grew revenue from an annualized ~$110 million to ~$125 million (approximately 14-15% increase) while actually reducing its total employee count compared to 2024, largely driven by AI and automation efficiencies.
Adjusted EBITDA expanded to $27.5 million for full year 2025 with a 23% margin, up more than 14% year-over-year, representing the highest adjusted EBITDA ever achieved by the company.

Through the Medsphere and MAP App acquisitions, CareCloud added more than 100 new hospital and health system relationships, creating a cross-selling runway for AI solutions and RCM services across the full care continuum.
The Board of Directors authorized a new $300 million stock repurchase program and increased the quarterly dividend by 12.5% to $0.09 per share ($0.36 per annum).

Cinemark fully extinguished all remaining COVID-related debt by settling final warrants related to convertible notes, with total settlement cost of $196 million ($98 million in cash and 3.6 million shares issued).
Q3 2025 global revenue was $857.5 million with adjusted EBITDA of $177.6 million, resulting in an adjusted EBITDA margin of 20.7%.

Cinemark achieved its highest third quarter domestic market share in company history, expanding market share by 40 basis points year-over-year and surpassing North American industry box office performance by nearly 250 basis points.
Domestic food and beverage per cap reached a new third quarter record of $8.20, an increase of 3% compared with Q3 2024.
Alternative content accounted for 16% of domestic box office in Q3, representing the company's second highest quarterly box office for non-traditional programming ever.
Global attendance was 54.2 million guests, a 10% decrease year-over-year reflecting a challenging comparison against 2024's strong film slate.
The company ended Q3 with $461 million in cash, a net leverage ratio of 2.4x (within target range of 2-3x), and nearest debt maturity not until 2028.
Average ticket price grew 5% year-over-year to $10.50, driven by strategic pricing actions and higher mix of alternative content.
Full-year 2025 capital expenditure target remains $225 million, with management indicating it is reasonable to anticipate some increase in CapEx for 2026.
Total second quarter revenues were $224.7 million, increasing 2.9% on a core basis, representing a return to positive core growth in both segments for the first time in 4 quarters.
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved 470 basis points sequentially to 21.7% in Q2, driven by higher gross margin and headcount reductions.
Cost structure improvements implemented in Q2 are expected to deliver approximately $20 million in annualized savings.
The company raised full year fiscal 2026 guidance to revenue of $845 million to $855 million and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $175 million.
Gross debt stood at $800 million with 68% at fixed rate and a cash position of $145.3 million at quarter end.

The negative impact from sample collection on gross profit improved from $10 million in Q4 to $6 million in Q1 to approximately $3 million in Q2, with expectations to turn positive in the second half.
Free cash flow in Q2 was $7.8 million, an improvement of $20.9 million from Q1, and routine CapEx is expected to trend towards 3% to 4% of revenue starting in late fiscal 2026.
The divestiture of the global genomics business is expected to be announced in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, with net proceeds prioritized for debt reduction.
Over 75% of food safety customers already purchase multiple product categories from Neogen, with targeted initiatives underway to increase cross-portfolio penetration.
Petrifilm integration remains on track for Q2 fiscal 2027, with the company currently in the latter stages of production testing and initial product validation for 17 SKUs.
Elevance Health reaffirmed 2025 adjusted EPS of approximately $30, with $27 as the appropriate earnings baseline excluding $3 of discrete nonrecurring items.
The company is planning for at least a 125 basis point year-over-year decline in Medicaid margins for 2026 as rates continue to lag acuity and utilization trends.
For the 2027 payment year, approximately 55% of Medicare Advantage members will be in 4-star or higher contracts, up from about 40% for payment year 2026.
Third quarter adjusted diluted earnings per share was $6.03 and GAAP diluted earnings per share was $5.32.
Total operating revenue for Q3 was $50.1 billion, up 12% year-over-year.
Full year 2025 Medicaid operating margin is now expected to be modestly negative at approximately negative 50 basis points.
Carelon Rx revenue grew 20% year-over-year while Carelon Services grew by more than 50% in the quarter.
The company repurchased $875 million of shares in the third quarter.
Medicare Advantage plan exits will impact approximately 150,000 members in 2026.
The company expects several hundred million dollars (approximately $1 of EPS) in incremental investments in 2026 focused on technology, Carelon expansion, and operational initiatives.
Q1 2026 product revenue was $53.7 million, up 24% year-over-year, driven by global platelet franchise strength and accelerating U.S. IFC demand.
Full-year 2026 product revenue guidance was raised to $227 million to $231 million, representing 10% to 12% year-over-year growth.
Full-year 2026 IFC revenue guidance was raised to $22 million to $24 million (from $20 million to $22 million), implying approximately 30% to 40% growth.
Q1 IFC revenue grew to $5.7 million versus $3.0 million in Q1 2025, with therapeutic dose equivalents up approximately 120% and revenue growth approaching 90% year-over-year.
North America accounted for nearly 70% of Q1 product revenue, with North American platelet volumes up 6% and treatable doses up 9% versus Q1 2025.

Q1 gross margin was 52% versus 58.8% a year ago (which included an ~2% one-time benefit), and full-year 2026 gross margin is expected to remain in the low 50s due to inflation, FX, and tariff headwinds.
EMEA revenue grew 28%, including approximately 11% benefit from favorable FX, with consolidated FX providing about a 3% benefit versus Q1 2025.
Q1 adjusted EBITDA was $4 million, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA, while GAAP net loss narrowed to $1.6 million.
Cash and equivalents ended Q1 at $80.4 million versus $82.9 million at year-end 2025, with $3 million cash used from operations tied to inventory investments.

The Phase III RedeS red blood cell study has completed enrollment with readout expected in Q4 2026, while the INT-200 PMA submission is planned for Q2 2026 with U.S. launch anticipated in the first half of 2027 and red cell CE Mark approval potentially in the first half of 2027.
Gross premiums written declined 15% year-over-year to $181 million from $212 million, primarily due to a reduction in new business writings, while earned premium was essentially flat (down 1%).
Adjusted net income fell to $10.3 million in Q1 2026 from $21.3 million a year ago.
The company returned $83 million to shareholders in Q1 2026 via share repurchases and dividends, following a record $215 million returned in 2025.

Employers repurchased over 1.8 million shares at an average price of $42.42 (a 17% discount to book value including deferred gain) for $76.9 million, plus an additional 353,547 shares at $42.21 between April 1-28, 2026.
The Board declared a Q2 2026 dividend of $0.34 per share (a 6.25% increase) and approved a new $125 million share repurchase authorization through December 31, 2027.
Book value per share including the deferred gain grew 8.9% to $51.26, and total capitalization stands at approximately $1 billion.
The current accident year loss and LAE ratio was 72%, consistent with 2025, and no prior-year reserve strengthening was required; the underwriting expense ratio improved to 22.6% from 23.4%.

Average renewal rate countrywide increased about 6% (with double-digit increases in California) while payrolls were up only 0.5%, and the California Bureau voted for a second consecutive double-digit pure premium rate increase.

The company completed a $125 million debt issuance ($105 million from FHLB and $20 million from credit facility) at a weighted-average pretax interest rate of 4.1%, and fixed maturity book yield rose to 4.9% from 4.5%.

Management expects the teens-level top-line decline to continue throughout 2026 as planned, with new growth initiatives (excess workers' comp, new agents, ChatGPT-integrated quoting) becoming visible toward year-end.
Q1 2026 EPS was $2.58 per diluted share on net income of $155.8 million, with an efficiency ratio of 63.2% and expenses down $6.9 million sequentially.
Total loans grew $536 million or 2.1% sequentially, with Texas up $208 million (8% annualized), Oklahoma up $163 million (~9% annualized), and Arizona up $236 million.
Full-year 2026 loan growth guidance is near 10%, with total revenue expected to grow mid-single digits and expenses in the low single digits, yielding a ~63% efficiency ratio.
NII guidance was lowered to $1.42–$1.45 billion and fee income raised to $820–$845 million, reflecting a revised assumption of zero rate cuts in 2026 versus two previously.

Net interest margin declined 8 basis points and core margin fell 7 bps due to seasonal DDA decline, lower loan fees, normalized SOFR spreads, energy derivative margin funding costs, and full-quarter impact of November sub debt.
Management estimates long-term margin could reach just over 3.15% (vs. 2.90% this quarter) as AFS and HTM securities reprice to ~4.50% maturity rates.

Credit remained exceptionally strong with net charge-offs of just $1.9 million (3 bps trailing 12-month average), NPAs down $14 million to $52 million (20 bps), no provision required, and 2026 provision guidance of $15–$35 million.
Energy loans grew 4.3% sequentially but management noted rig counts are down 40+ from a year ago and customers won't drill until the 3-year strip exceeds ~$70 oil.

Fee income totaled $209.8 million (down $5.1 million sequentially), with Q1 2026 representing the strongest first-quarter syndication activity on record, up 40% year-over-year, and fiduciary/asset management revenue of $66.5 million (second strongest ever) despite AUMA declining $3 billion to $123.6 billion.

Visa's second Class B exchange program commenced April 13, allowing BOKF to monetize half of its ~190,000 common-share-equivalent position for an estimated ~$29 million pretax gain (not included in guidance), with capital levels at 9.3% TCE and 12.6% CET1.
Q3 2025 total revenue was $116 million, up 30% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $55 million (up 37% YoY) achieving a record 47% margin.
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $191-193 million (implying >43% margin), while reaffirming revenue growth of 26% or greater.
Direct revenue grew 25% year-over-year while indirect revenue (primarily advertising) grew 56% year-over-year in Q3.
Average paying users reached 1.3 million in Q3 with a penetration rate of 8.6%, up from approximately 6.5% three years ago.
Year-to-date share repurchases totaled 25.1 million shares for approximately $450 million, leaving $50 million remaining under current authorization.
Subscription price testing (first since 2018) showed de minimis impact on paying user base with retention exceeding the company's most optimistic projections.
A new AI-powered premium tier for power users is being tested, with meaningful revenue expected beginning late 2026 and accelerating in 2027.
Q3 free cash flow was approximately $51 million, with net income of $31 million ($0.16 per diluted share) compared to $25 million ($0.09 per share) a year ago.
Management expects 2026-2027 EBITDA margins to be in the 39-42% range due to continued AI and product investments, despite finishing 2025 above 43%.
Users aged 18-29 comprise 46% of U.S. Grindr profiles (versus 9% of U.S. adult male population), and approximately 350,000 users subscribe to the Unlimited tier.
Q3 2025 revenue increased 6% to $263 million while adjusted EBITDA grew 10% to $87 million.
Comparable store sales growth of 3.1% marks the tenth consecutive quarter of positive comp gains.
UWC membership reached approximately 2.2 million members, a 6% year-over-year increase, with Titanium 360 tier reaching 25% penetration of the total membership base.
Adjusted EPS was $0.11, representing a 38% increase year-over-year.
Q3 EBITDA margin of 32.9% represents the highest Q3 EBITDA margin the company has ever reported.
Outstanding long-term debt was reduced by more than $100 million over the last 12 months, bringing the leverage ratio to 2.4x adjusted EBITDA.
Free cash flow for the nine months ended September 30 was $202 million, representing 26% of sales, compared to $174 million in the prior year period.
New competitor store openings within a 3-mile radius of existing Mister Car Wash locations have declined an estimated 40% year-to-date versus last year.
The company expects 100% bonus depreciation and existing net operating losses to reduce federal cash tax liability to near zero for the next several years.

Full year 2025 guidance is reiterated with comparable store sales expected at the high end or slightly above the 1.5% to 2.5% range, and adjusted EBITDA expected at the high end of $338 million to $342 million.

Black Rock delivered full year 2025 revenue of $200.3 million, representing 24.5% year-over-year growth, and adjusted EBITDA of $27.5 million, representing 36.2% growth with margin expanding 120 basis points to 13.7%.
Same-store sales grew 10.1% for full year 2025 and 9.3% in Q4, representing a 2-year stack of 16.4% and 18.8% respectively, with Q4 same-store transaction growth of 4.2%.
The company opened 32 new stores in 2025 (ahead of the 30-unit plan), ending the year with 181 total stores, and guided for 36 new store openings in 2026.

For 2026, the company guided total revenue of $255 million to $257 million, mid-single-digit same-store sales growth, adjusted EBITDA of $33.5 million to $34.5 million, and capital expenditures of $40 million to $41 million including tenant improvement allowances.
Store level profit margin expanded to 29.2% for full year 2025 (up from 27.9% prior year) and reached 29.4% in Q4 (230 basis points favorable year-over-year).

Beverage, food and packaging costs improved 190 basis points year-over-year to 27.4% of revenue in Q4, while coffee costs remained elevated through Q4 and into early 2026 with anticipated relief in the second half of the year.

The loyalty rewards program, launched in June 2024, has grown to approximately 2 million members with a 65% participation rate, with loyalty members visiting more often and spending more per visit than non-loyalty members.
System-wide average unit volume reached $1.3 million, with the 2025 new unit cohort exceeding sales forecasts and delivering strong store level margin acceleration and cash-on-cash returns.
As of December 31, 2025, the company had $28.4 million in cash, $26.7 million in total debt, a net cash position of $9.7 million, and access to a $25 million unfunded revolver.

The company reaffirmed its long-term targets of 20% annual new unit growth, 20%+ revenue growth, mid-single-digit same-store sales growth, and EBITDA growth outpacing revenue, with a goal of reaching 1,000 units by 2035.
Gen Digital reported FY26 revenue of $5.0 billion (up 27% reported, 9% pro forma) and non-GAAP EPS of $2.56 (up 15%), marking 10 consecutive quarters within its 12%-15% EPS growth commitment.

Q4 FY26 bookings were $1.36 billion (up 27% reported, 10% pro forma) and revenue was $1.28 billion (up 27% reported, 9% pro forma), with diluted EPS of $0.67 beating guidance and growing 14% year-over-year.

Gen raised its FY27 outlook to 8%-10% pro forma revenue growth ($5.325B-$5.425B) and 13%-17% EPS growth ($2.85-$2.95), a structural step-up from prior mid-single-digit revenue and 12%-15% EPS growth targets.

The company exited FY26 at 3x net leverage, a year ahead of schedule, with $411 million cash, nearly $2 billion liquidity including a $1.5B revolver, and refinanced its Term Loan A at SOFR+1.375% extending maturities to 2031.
Cyber Safety segment grew bookings 5% and revenue 3% pro forma in FY26 at a 61% segment margin, while Trust-Based Solutions grew bookings 24% and revenue 23% pro forma at a 30% margin.
Paid customer count reached 79 million (up from 68 million a year ago), with cohort-level ARPU now 7%-10% higher than two years ago and Norton cross-sell penetration exceeding 26% of the base.

Higher-tier Norton 360 memberships including scam detection, identity protection and insurance surpassed $0.5 billion in annualized bookings, with membership adoption approaching 60% across Norton, Avast, and Avira.

MoneyLion grew over 40% in FY26 (nearly 40% in Q4), is approaching $1 billion in annual revenue, with connected financial accounts up 36% year-over-year to 107 million and one-third of the paid base engaging with financial wellness.

LifeLock's reimagined experience reached approximately 3 million customers with NPS at 73 (up 4 points), retention near 90%, mobile revenue up nearly 50%, and linked financial monitoring accounts up nearly 25%.

Gen generated $1.5 billion in free cash flow in FY26 (over 30% of revenue, up 26%), deployed nearly $500 million in Q4 including $200M buybacks (9M shares) and $200M debt repayment, with $2.1 billion remaining on share repurchase authorization.
Q1 2026 net income was $30.5 million or $0.18 per share, up from $26.7 million or $0.15 per share in Q1 2025, but core EPS declined to $0.18 from $0.23 year-over-year.

HEI made the first of four annual $479 million Maui wildfire settlement payments on April 10, 2026, using funds previously set aside in a special purpose vehicle, with remaining payments due April 2027, 2028, and 2029.
Management plans to fund the second settlement payment with debt and/or convertible debt, with subsequent payments funded by a mix of debt and equity, while targeting investment-grade credit metrics.

Moody's upgraded the utility one notch to Ba1 (one notch below investment grade) and the holding company to Ba2 following the settlement finalization, with S&P and Fitch maintaining positive outlooks.

The joint rate rebasing proposal with Ulupono Initiative seeks a consolidated base rate increase of approximately 5.3% phased over two years, adding $8–$12 to average customer bills in 2027 and $2–$3 more in 2028.
